court: In the High Court of Madras
sections_referred: Order IX, Rule 9 of Civil Procedure Code, 1908
advocates: For Respondent(s): Mr. V. Ramesh, G.A., for R 3
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

P.B. Balaji, J.:— Heard Mr. S. Rajasekar, learned counsel for the petitioner. Mr. V. Ramesh, learned Government Advocate, takes notice for the third respondent.

2. The suit filed by the petitioner was dismissed for default on 04.04.2025. An application was immediately filed for restoration of the suit invoking Order IX, Rule 9 of CPC in I.A. No. 4 of 2025. The grievance of the petitioner is that the said application has not been disposed of for more than one year and the delay is causing serious prejudice.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner brings to my notice that the petitioner was enjoying the interim order pending suit and taking advantage of the dismissal of the suit, now the respondent has filed a fresh suit, which has been entertained before the same Court. He would also bring to my notice that I.A. is now posted on 03.03.2026 and pleadings are already completed.

4. In the light of the above, I am inclined to dispense with notice to the respondents and allow the Civil Revision Petition. The learned District Munsif-cum-Judicial Magistrate is directed to dispose of I.A.4 of 2025 on or before 13.03.2026. Accordingly, the Civil Revision Petition is allowed. No costs.
